From embedded design knowledge to measurable form.Concept prototype · v1.0

2006 → 2026

Twenty years ahead.
Still an unfinished idea.

Shouheng Chen’s Embedding Methods for Massing and Detail Design in Computer Generated Design of Skyscrapers (MIT, June 2006) embeds design conventions into reusable rules. Profiles, transition levels, scaling and rotation generate massing; relationships between neighboring points generate façade components.

This studio extends that approach with interior and value proxies. Chen explicitly identifies interior programs and structural and ecological performance as future work in chapter 6. The financial model here is a new extension; it is not a finding of the thesis.

What is computed

Every slab uses a transformed polygon. Gross area is its polygon area; the fixed square core and a percentage allowance for circulation/services are deducted to get rentable area. The selected floor highlights candidate corner offices.

A corner qualifies when it is convex, its angle is ≤145°, both adjoining edges are at least twice the chosen frontage, and its inward parallelogram fits without touching the core. This spacing keeps adjacent corner zones apart. These are possible office footprints, not a finished tenancy plan.

Annual rent = (rentable area + corner area × premium) × base annual rent × occupancy.
Annual contribution = annual rent − façade area × annual envelope reserve.

Façade area sums triangulated faces between successive profiles, including taper and twist. It excludes structural cost and glazing detail. Contribution excludes operating costs, financing, tax and capital costs. It is neither net operating income nor a valuation.

How alternatives are compared

Search tests 5 profiles × 4 roof scales (1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7) × 4 twists (0°, 30°, 60°, 90°). Each is resized to the current gross floor area, keeping floors, core, aspect and commercial assumptions fixed. Equal gross area with fixed floors, core and allowance also fixes rentable area; the value differences come from corner premiums and façade area. Candidates outside the envelope, above the height limit or with a core outside the floor plate are rejected. This is a bounded search, not a global optimum.

Where architecture still needs judgment

No structural, egress, accessibility, wind, daylight, thermal or local planning-code solver is included. The core is a conceptual allowance; an engineer and architect must size it. Diagrids illustrate associative detail and do not prove structural performance. All financial inputs are illustrative user-editable assumptions, not live market data.
